title.narrative: Response to support families in Chocó affected by floods, gales and landslides

description.narrative:
CAFODs partners the Diocese of Choco and COCOMOPOCA are responding to the humanitarian emergency caused by the heavy rains that occurred on April 20, eleven municipalities in the department of Chocó were affected by floods, gales and / or landslides. Initial report estimated that at least 2,083 families would be affected in 8 municipalities. The flooding destroyed crops and livelihood, including in areas where CAFOD has a project with the AfroColombian communities of COCOMPOCA. COCOMOPOCA accounted for 2553 families in 36 AfroColombian communities affected.
Although there was an initial response from the Colombia’s government providing food and non-food items. There are concerns about the more mid to long term impact as the floods destroyed crops and the communities living next to the river have lost their livelihood.
The project aims to work with 200 families (about 800 people) in 15 communities (8 in the municipality of Lloro and 7 in the municipality of Atrato). It focus on those most affected in the AfroColombian communities living close to the Atrato River and depending on farming the land next to the river. The main component of the project is related to the buying and planting of seeds for manioc and plantain. An agricultural professional will be hired to advise the communities. (Traditionally they plant the crops next to the river, but that is not advisable due to the increased frequency of flooding related to climate change, so the technical advice would focus on this). A small component of the project will be looking at the Risk Management Plan of COCOMOPOCA developed with the support of the Lutheran World Federation in 2014 and discussing with these communities why it is not working, if they need to adapt it and how they can implement it effectively.
